_about: Curated qualitative context used ONLY as hypotheses in explanations. Not used in any score. Each note cites where to verify it. Verify before relying on it.

SFO.note: SFO's two pairs of parallel runways are closely spaced (about 750 ft apart). In low ceilings / poor visibility, side-by-side arrivals are restricted, which substantially cuts the arrival rate - a well-documented driver of SFO ground-delay programs.
SFO.source: FAA Airport Capacity Profiles; SFO airport publications

SFO.note: Airfield expansion is physically constrained by San Francisco Bay, so added runway capacity is not a realistic near-term lever; terminal / gate and airspace-procedure improvements are the more plausible levers.

SNA.note: John Wayne Airport operates under a court-approved Settlement Agreement that caps annual passengers and regulated daily departures, plus a nighttime noise curfew. Capacity is policy-constrained, not only physically constrained, which limits the upside of terminal expansion.

LAX.note: LAX already has a multi-billion-dollar modernization program underway (Landside Access Modernization Program, terminal redevelopments). Existing committed capital affects how much incremental opportunity remains for a new investor.

ANC.note: ANC is one of the world's busiest all-cargo airports. Passenger enplanements and reporting-carrier passenger flights do not capture its cargo-driven airfield activity.

BOS.note: Logan is surrounded by Boston Harbor and dense neighborhoods, so airfield expansion is land-constrained; recent investment has focused on terminals and gates (e.g., Terminal E).
